newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dlr ends weaker despite bank intervention.
newsitem.headline: Canada dlr ends weaker despite bank intervention.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended sharply weaker around C$1.3944 (US$0.7171) on Tuesday from Monday's close at C$1.3882 (US$0.7203), despite Bank of Canada intervention * Traders said central bank intervened around C$1.3940 level after heavy selling by the International Monetary Market * Investors looking ahead to Canada merchandise trade data on Wednesday

Traders said tame Canadian inflation data released on Tuesday reduces the likelihood of a interest rate hike from the Bank of Canada. Currency traders have put pressure on the Canadian dollar recently to test the central bank's resolve.

Canada's unadjusted July consumer price index was unchanged in the month and rose 1.8 percent in the year, Statistics Canada said on Tuesday. Economists in a Reuters survey had forecast, on average, that unadjusted CPI would rise 0.1 percent on the month. "What this does is, it delays the immediate need for a rate hike from the Bank of Canada," said Goldman Sachs senior economist Mark Chandler.

"It doesn't get much better in Canada. Economic activity is on the upswing while price pressures are on the downswing," Scotiabank said in a commentary on Tuesday. But it added the weak link in Canada's outlook is the currency.

"The exchange rate has had a hard time keeping its head above US$0.72, though lower inflation, stronger growth and substantially reduced government borrowing requirements should eventually be good news for the (currency)," Scotiabank said.
Looking ahead to Wednesday, Statistics Canada is expected to report Canada's international trade and wholesale trade figures for June.
"I don't think the expectation is for a wild swing so I don't think the market is going to be overly focused on it (the trade data)," said one trader at a Canadian bank.
On the crosses, the Canada dollar edged up to 84.74 Japanese yen from 84.66 yen on Monday and dipped to 1.3199 marks from 1.3209 marks on Monday.
